claims.text: Upon the death of his father, Pelendur, the Stewardship of Gondor became hereditary within the House of Húrin and thus Vorondil succeeded to the position.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "Gondor and the Heirs of Anárion", "The Stewards"

claims.text: Early in Vorondil's Stewardship Gondor was attacked and suffered a serious defeat. In , the Nazgûl issued from Mordor to besiege Minas Ithil. The city fell in and with it they took the Palantír therein.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix B, "The Third Age"

claims.text: Vorondil was remembered as "Vorondil the Hunter" for his hunting of the Kine of Araw, found near the shores of the Sea of Rhûn. From one of the wild white oxen he fashioned a Great Horn, bound with silver and written with characters. It had been passed to the eldest son for generations within the House of Húrin and Boromir was the last to carry this horn.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "The Realms in Exile", "The Southern Line: Heirs of Anarion"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Two Towers, "The Window on the West"; J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, The Return of the King, "The Tower of Cirith Ungol"

claims.text: Vorondil was succeeded by his son Mardil, who would become the first of the Ruling Stewards.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, The Lord of the Rings, Appendix A, "The Númenorean Kings", "Gondor and the Heirs of Anárion", "The Stewards"
